route: explicit code labels in the source (Step 5b exemption 2), corroborated by route 1 (published per-item loadings)
evidence: Supplementary Material 1 of Gan et al. 2022 (file Table_2.DOCX) prints a Labels x Measurement items table; 4/4 codes matched verbatim to the shipped text ('SWLS1 | In the most ways my life is close to my ideal', 'SWLS2 | The conditions of my life are excellent', 'SWLS3 | I am satisfied with my life', 'SWLS4 | So far, I have gotten the important things I want in life'), and data/kern_2021_positive_edu.py melts the figshare workbook by column name so item == header (row 1 cols 34-37 read SWLS1,SWLS2,SWLS3,SWLS4). Every item is therefore distinguished from every other by a code-to-text label match. Corroboration only: paper Table 2 outer loadings 0.860/0.831/0.884/0.763 vs live one-factor loadings 0.762/0.799/0.881/0.655 (n=350) reproduce SWLS3 highest and SWLS4 lowest but REVERSE the 0.03-wide SWLS1-vs-SWLS2 gap, so the loading route on its own does NOT separate SWLS1 from SWLS2; the label match is what does. Option/resp axis: only the two endpoint anchors are published, and direction (1=Strongly disagree) rests on the raw workbook's SWLS total correlating +0.557 with the SHS total whose anchors run 'Not a very happy person'(low) to 'A very happy person'(high).

route: 1 (per-item published response counts) + 9 (response-frequency matching for the option/resp axis)
evidence: Paper Table 2 prints Agree/Disagree n for each of the four attitude statements and all four Agree counts are distinct: 342 / 362 / 296 / 118. Live per-item resp==1 counts are 342 (attitude1), 362 (attitude2), 296 (attitude3), 118 (attitude5) and resp==2 counts are 58 / 38 / 104 / 282, matching the published Disagree counts exactly, all four items, n=400 each. Because the four counts differ, any permutation of item_text across the four items breaks the match, and the reversed reading (1=Disagree) fits none of them - so this also fixes the coding direction against the questionnaire's own '(1) Strongly Disagree' annotation. What it does NOT establish: the wording itself, which is transcribed verbatim from supplement s004.docx and is checked only by the paper's Table 2 column headers reproducing the same four statements.

Paper's 'Clinical Readiness & Emergency Response Capacity' table publishes Yes n (%) per item: 1 protocol 178 (44.5), 2 emergency kit 232 (58.0), 3 AED 30 (7.5), 4 refresher interest 244 (61.0), N=400. Live irw_fetch counts of resp==1 per item: cr1 178 (44.5%), cr2 232 (58.0%), cr3 30 (7.5%), cr4 61.0% = 244 -- exact on all four. The four published counts are mutually distinct, so the route separates every item from every other item; a swap of any pair would land on the wrong count. It does not speak to the confidence items 5-8 printed in the same source section, which are the separate khattak_2026_confidence table. Option mapping Yes=1/No=2 is independently fixed by the s001.sav value labels for cr1-cr4 and by the SPSS codes printed in supplement s004.

route: 5 (subscale block structure) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution)
evidence: Live irw_fetch, n=1335, 17 items. Canonical AMS three-factor assignment (psychological 6,7,8,11,13; somato-vegetative 1,2,3,4,5,9,10; sexual 12,14,15,16,17): 14/17 items' highest-correlating partner sits in their own subscale; mean within-subscale r = 0.537 vs mean between-subscale r = 0.431. The three misses are Q03 (nearest Q08, r=0.457), Q12 (nearest Q09, r=0.638) and Q14 (nearest Q08, r=0.578) -- items 12 and 14 are the AMS's known weak sexual-subscale markers. The three explicitly sexual items form a closed triad: r(Q15,Q17)=0.841, r(Q16,Q17)=0.838, r(Q15,Q16)=0.767, each item's top-2 correlates are the other two (next best is Q12 at 0.516/0.554/0.565), and they are the three highest item means (Q17=3.001, Q15=2.972, Q16=2.955 vs 4th Q12=2.718). Corroborating the numbering from the source paper's own prose: item 4 = 'one single item for sleep' (AMS 4 sleep problems), item 14 = 'one single item that had been generally ignored' (AMS 14 beard growth, the lowest mean at 1.855), item 17 = 'one single item most central to the AMS' (AMS 17 libido, the highest mean at 3.001). NOT established: the order of items within a subscale -- nothing here separates Q06/Q07/Q08 (irritability/nervousness/anxiety, mutual r 0.748-0.751) or Q15 from Q16. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: 7 (marker item, cross-instrument) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution)
evidence: Cross-instrument content correlations over the same 202 respondents (verify_kim_2023_gad7.R): corr(gad_i, PHQ9_8), the PHQ-9's only psychomotor-restlessness item, is highest for gad5 at 0.657 against 0.546/0.533/0.477/0.534/0.332/0.566 for gad1/2/3/4/6/7, and PHQ9_8 is reciprocally gad5's strongest PHQ-9 correlate (0.657 vs 0.455 0.560 0.535 0.417 0.384 0.598 0.481 0.480). gad6 is simultaneously the weakest correlate of PHQ9_8 (0.332) and the strongest correlate of PSS_9, the PSS-10 anger item (0.506 vs 0.438 0.371 0.480 0.458 0.412 0.358). Item means 1.07 (gad3) > 1.00 (gad6) > 0.78 > 0.69 > 0.66 > 0.49 (gad5) > 0.46 (gad7) corroborate: the generic worry item highest, restlessness and fear-of-something-awful lowest. Option axis separately settled by the instrument: the GAD-7 form prints 0/1/2/3 beside its four anchors, and in the deposit gad_T equals the raw sum of gad1..gad7 exactly (max abs diff 0.0, range 0-21). NOT ESTABLISHED: this route pins gad5 and gad6 only; gad1, gad2, gad3, gad4 and gad7 are not distinguished from one another, because none has a comparably specific content twin in the PHQ-9 or PSS-10. Hence PARTIAL.
